paragraphs: Behavioral cloning teaches an agent to reproduce expert actions in situations covered by demonstrations. A mistake can push the agent into unfamiliar situations where those examples offer little guidance. SAILOR addresses this recovery problem by learning components that let an agent search for ways to achieve expert outcomes during deployment.

The approach learns both a world model and a reward model from expert demonstrations. These components support planning: anticipating what actions might do and evaluating whether their outcomes match the intended behavior. The researchers systematically examine design choices needed to combine these components into stable learning that uses samples and interactions efficiently, without requiring additional human corrections.

Across twelve visual manipulation tasks from three benchmarks, SAILOR consistently outperforms leading Diffusion Policies trained through behavioral cloning on the same data. Increasing the cloning demonstrations by five to ten times still leaves a performance gap. The authors also find that SAILOR detects subtle failures and resists reward hacking, supporting the value of learning recovery through search in the evaluated tasks.
neurips-2025-a-smooth-sea-never-made-a-s.tldr: SAILOR learns models for planning from demonstrations, improving recovery and manipulation performance over behavioral cloning in the evaluated tasks.

paragraphs: This paper asks whether transformers need increasingly precise numbers or more parameters to represent computations on longer inputs. The authors prove that a transformer with constant bit size can simulate any Turing machine on arbitrarily long inputs, provided its context window is sufficiently long. The context requirement is essential to the stated result.

The proof works through Post machines, a computational model that combines an automaton with a queue. These machines are computationally universal, and their queue-based behavior fits naturally with transformer computation. Simulating them lets the authors establish universality without increasing model precision or parameter count as input length grows.

The paper also connects context length to a precise computational resource: space. It proves that a context window of length s(n) gives exactly the expressive power characterized by SPACE[s(n)]. This makes context capacity central to the theoretical account. The authors suggest that the similarity to Post machines could help explain transformer reasoning, while presenting that connection as a possible insight rather than an established explanation of trained models.
neurips-2025-constant-bit-size-transform.tldr: Constant-bit-size transformers can simulate arbitrary Turing machines given sufficient context, with context length precisely characterizing their space complexity.

paragraphs: The paper studies a limitation of using eluder dimension to analyze sequential learning. Its first result is a lower bound for classes of generalized linear models. That bound shows that standard analyses based on eluder dimension cannot deliver first-order regret guarantees, establishing a barrier for this particular theoretical approach.

The proposed remedy is to localize the eluder dimension. Rather than abandon the complexity measure, the authors change how it enters the analysis so that the resulting guarantees can be more responsive to the learning problem. The key contribution is therefore both diagnostic and constructive: it identifies why an established analysis falls short and supplies a method that gets beyond that obstacle.

The localized analysis recovers and improves classic results for Bernoulli bandits. It also yields what the authors describe as the first genuine first-order bounds for finite-horizon reinforcement learning with bounded cumulative returns. That qualification defines the reinforcement learning setting covered by the claim. Together, the results show that localization can strengthen guarantees across both bandit and reinforcement learning problems.
neurips-2025-eluder-dimension-localise-i.tldr: Localizing eluder dimension overcomes a barrier in standard analyses and yields stronger bandit and bounded-return reinforcement learning guarantees.

paragraphs: Tabular foundation models such as TabPFN can adapt to new tasks through examples supplied in context. However, their architectures often assume a fixed number of target dimensions. The paper connects this restriction to a deeper problem: changing the order of target dimensions can change predictions in ways that should not depend on that ordering.

The authors describe the resulting instability as an irreducible equivariance gap. EquiTabPFN removes this gap through an architecture whose encoders, decoders, and bi-attention mechanism respect permutations of target dimensions. Intuitively, rearranging the targets should produce the corresponding rearrangement of outputs while preserving the underlying prediction. Building this behavior into the architecture addresses the source of the ordering problem.

On standard classification benchmarks, the model matches or exceeds existing methods when datasets contain more classes than were encountered during pretraining. It also uses less computation in those evaluations. These findings connect the architectural guarantee to a practical benefit: handling larger target sets with lower overhead, in a setting where existing approaches often rely on costly ensembles.
neurips-2025-equitabpfn-a-target-permuta.tldr: EquiTabPFN removes target-ordering instability and handles more classes than seen in pretraining with competitive accuracy and lower computational overhead.

paragraphs: EVAAA is a three-dimensional environment for studying reinforcement learning agents whose behavior is driven by internal needs. Its motivation is that conventional environments often provide fixed tasks and externally specified goals, whereas biological agents must continuously adapt their behavior to remain viable under changing conditions.

Agents in EVAAA maintain internal variables such as satiation, hydration, body temperature, and tissue integrity within viable ranges. Rewards come from changes in these internal states, allowing goals to arise from the agent's condition without separately engineering a reward for each task. The environment becomes harder across training stages, connecting physiological regulation to increasingly demanding survival situations.

Built with Unity ML-Agents, the platform supports first-person embodiment and sensory inputs including vision, smell, temperature, and collisions. It combines environments for staged training with unseen test settings for evaluating adaptation. The contribution is a benchmark platform that brings internal regulation, embodiment, continual learning, and generalization into the same experimental setting, enabling study of how autonomous behavior emerges from internal needs and environmental constraints.
neurips-2025-evaaa-a-virtual-environment.tldr: EVAAA provides virtual survival environments where embodied agents learn from internal physiological needs and face unseen tests of adaptation.

paragraphs: Dataset distillation aims to create a compact dataset that remains useful for training models. FADRM approaches this task by moving the idea of residual connections from model architecture into data generation. Its data-level skip connections help retain information from the original data while the distilled examples are optimized.

The method balances knowledge acquired through pixel-space optimization with core local information already present in the raw data. This is intended to reduce information loss during generation. Additional changes to the optimization procedure improve efficiency, with the paper reporting reductions of 50% in both training time and peak GPU memory use alongside stronger performance.

The authors report leading results across multiple dataset benchmarks. On ImageNet-1K, using ResNet-18 and a 0.8% compression ratio, FADRM reaches 47.7% test accuracy for single-model distillation and 50.0% for multi-model distillation. These examples make the contribution concrete: preserving useful original-data information can improve the quality of a very small training set while reducing the resources needed to produce it.
neurips-2025-fadrm-fast-and-accurate-dat.tldr: FADRM uses data-level residual connections to improve dataset distillation while reporting 50% reductions in training time and peak GPU memory.

paragraphs: MM-UPT explores how multimodal language models can keep improving after supervised fine-tuning and reinforcement learning without additional external supervision. The motivation is the cost of manually labeled multimodal training data. The proposed framework uses the model's own sampled answers to provide a training signal.

The training procedure builds on GRPO, replacing conventional rewards with a self-rewarding mechanism based on majority voting across multiple responses. This allows training on existing datasets without their ground-truth labels. With Qwen2.5-VL-7B, the reported results improve from 66.3% to 72.9% on MathVista and from 62.9% to 68.7% on We-Math, showing gains in the evaluated reasoning tasks.

The authors also investigate generating the training inputs themselves. They design two prompting strategies through which the model synthesizes new examples, then combine those examples with the same unsupervised training procedure. Additional experiments show performance improvements from this combination. Together, the results support self-generated rewards and data as a promising route to further post-training, with the demonstrated gains grounded in the tested model and tasks.
neurips-2025-first-sft-second-rl-third-u.tldr: MM-UPT improves tested multimodal reasoning performance using majority-vote self-rewards and, optionally, model-generated training examples.

paragraphs: HawkBench evaluates whether retrieval-augmented generation systems can handle different kinds of information needs. The paper argues that benchmarks dominated by short factual questions give an incomplete picture of this adaptability. Users also ask questions that require explanations and reasoning, so evaluation needs to distinguish among these behaviors.

The benchmark contains 1,600 human-labeled test examples evenly distributed across domains and task types. It includes both factual and rationale questions, uses multi-domain corpora across task categories to reduce corpus-related bias, and applies rigorous annotation. This structure makes task differences a deliberate part of evaluation, rather than allowing them to become entangled with entirely different knowledge sources.

The researchers assess representative retrieval-augmented methods using answer quality and response latency. Their findings point toward strategies that adapt to the task by combining decision-making, query interpretation, and an understanding of the broader knowledge available. HawkBench therefore contributes both an evaluation resource and evidence that general-purpose information seeking requires attention to how user needs vary across queries.
neurips-2025-hawkbench-investigating-res.tldr: HawkBench tests retrieval-augmented systems across diverse information needs, highlighting the importance of task-adaptive strategies.

paragraphs: Models that combine image understanding and image generation do not necessarily perform equally well at both. The authors identify a common pattern in multimodal language models: their understanding ability is usually stronger than their ability to generate. HermesFlow is designed to reduce this imbalance within a unified model.

The framework builds related preference data for understanding and generation from corresponding source data. This connects the two learning objectives through a shared basis for judging better and worse responses. HermesFlow then uses Pair-DPO together with iterative self-play optimization to align the two capabilities, making their relationship an explicit part of training.

The reported experiments show substantial improvements over prior methods, particularly in narrowing the gap between understanding and generation. This matters because progress on one capability alone may leave a unified model unevenly capable across its intended uses. The findings support HermesFlow as a possible general alignment framework for multimodal foundation models, with that broader role presented as potential rather than a guarantee across every model.
neurips-2025-hermesflow-seamlessly-closi.tldr: HermesFlow uses paired preference learning and iterative self-play to narrow the observed gap between multimodal understanding and generation.

paragraphs: KungfuBot tackles humanoid imitation of rapid, demanding human movements such as Kungfu and dancing. These motions create challenges beyond tracking smooth, slow demonstrations. The framework addresses both the preparation of human motion data and the way a robot learns to follow that motion under physical constraints.

Its processing pipeline extracts motions, filters unsuitable material, corrects motions, and retargets them to the robot while seeking the greatest possible physical compatibility. During learning, a bi-level optimization procedure adjusts the allowed tracking error according to the policy's current performance. This creates an adaptive curriculum: tracking demands change as the robot learns. Policy training also uses an asymmetric actor-critic framework.

In experiments with a collection of highly dynamic motions, the resulting whole-body policies achieve substantially lower tracking errors than existing approaches. The researchers also deploy the controller on a Unitree G1 robot, where it produces stable and expressive behavior. These results connect improvements in motion tracking to demonstrated physical execution, supporting the combination of careful motion preparation and adaptive training.
neurips-2025-kungfubot-physics-based-hum.tldr: KungfuBot combines motion processing and adaptive tracking to learn dynamic humanoid skills and demonstrate them on a Unitree G1.

paragraphs: This paper investigates whether a language model's eventual behavior can sometimes be predicted before it generates any output. The researchers train probes on internal representations of input tokens. These probes predict properties of the eventual response, including alignment and instruction-following failures that would otherwise be identified after generation.

The method uses conformal prediction to provide provable bounds on probe estimation error. An early warning system built from these probes reduces jailbreaking by 91% in the reported evaluation. The probes also show promise for predicting how confident the model will be in its response, a property the authors say cannot be detected from output text alone.

A further application predicts the final classification from a model using chain-of-thought prompting, reducing the need to complete its reasoning output. Across 27 classification datasets, this cuts inference costs by 65% on average with negligible accuracy loss. Generalization to unseen datasets and better performance on larger models suggest broader applicability, while the central claim remains that early prediction works for some behaviors and instances.
neurips-2025-language-models-can-predict.tldr: Probes of input representations can anticipate some language-model behaviors before generation, enabling early warnings and cheaper classification.

paragraphs: Molecular coordinate denoising trains models to recover structures after atomic positions are perturbed. The paper argues that common noise models simplify molecular motion too much by treating directions equally and using uniform variability. AniDS replaces those assumptions with noise that depends on each atom and its structural surroundings.

Its noise generator produces a full Gaussian covariance matrix for each atom, allowing perturbations to vary by direction. Pairwise atomic interactions provide directional corrections to an isotropic starting point. The construction ensures mathematically valid covariance matrices and rotation-equivariant behavior, so rotating a structure rotates its noise description consistently. This gives the denoising model greater capacity to represent structured molecular variability.

On MD17 and OC22, AniDS outperforms prior denoising models and other leading methods, with reported average relative improvements in force prediction accuracy of 8.9% and 6.2%. A crystal and molecule case study finds reduced noise along bond directions, consistent with physicochemical principles. The results support using structurally informed directional noise to improve molecular representation learning and force prediction.
neurips-2025-learning-3d-anisotropic-noi.tldr: AniDS learns atom-specific directional noise for molecular denoising, improving force prediction on MD17 and OC22.

paragraphs: Logic.py divides logic-puzzle solving between a language model and a constraint solver. The language model translates the problem into a formal representation, and the solver finds a solution to that representation. This gives the model a focused role in expressing the problem's rules before a dedicated tool handles the search.

The intermediate representation is a human-readable, logic-focused domain-specific language called Logic.py. Its purpose is to connect natural-language problem descriptions with the formal constraints a solver can use. This separation matters because the system can draw on the language model's ability to interpret a description while assigning constraint satisfaction to a tool built for that operation.

On ZebraLogicBench, the approach improves Llama 3.1 70B's baseline accuracy by 65 percentage points and achieves accuracy above 90%, which the authors report as a new state of the art. The result provides evidence that formalization through a suitable language can substantially improve performance on search-based problems that are difficult for language models to solve directly.
neurips-2025-logic-py-bridging-the-gap-b.tldr: Logic.py has language models formalize puzzles for a constraint solver, achieving over 90% accuracy on ZebraLogicBench.

paragraphs: MJ-Bench evaluates the models that judge text-to-image outputs and provide feedback for improving generators. Poor judgments can guide training toward undesirable behavior, so the benchmark examines judging ability across alignment, safety, image quality, bias, composition, and visualization. Its preference dataset breaks these perspectives into more specific evaluation categories.

The study compares compact CLIP-based scoring models, open-source vision-language models, and closed-source vision-language models. Closed-source models generally give better feedback, with GPT-4o performing best on average. However, compact scoring models can outperform open-source vision-language models on text-image alignment and image quality. Vision-language models provide more accurate safety and bias feedback, which the authors attribute to stronger reasoning abilities.

The format of feedback also matters: vision-language judges generally give more accurate and stable assessments in natural language than on numerical scales. Human evaluations of end-to-end and fine-tuned systems using these judges' feedback lead to similar conclusions. This agreement supports the benchmark's usefulness for assessing judges and shows why judge selection should consider the particular quality being evaluated.
neurips-2025-mj-bench-is-your-multimodal.tldr: MJ-Bench reveals that image-generation judges have different strengths across quality dimensions and often give better feedback in natural language.

paragraphs: MyoChallenge 2024 benchmarks coordinated control of biological and prosthetic limbs. It is motivated by the adaptability of people who integrate bionic devices into their movements, a capability the authors describe as beyond current artificial intelligence systems. The benchmark makes this coordination problem concrete through two simulated tasks.

The manipulation track uses myoMPL, combining a virtual biological arm with a Modular Prosthetic Limb for a passover task. The locomotion track uses myoOSL, a model incorporating a transfemoral amputation and an Open Source Leg, to navigate varied terrain. Both tracks require controllers to address biological and mechanical components within the same movement problem.

More than 50 teams contributed over 290 submissions. The competition produced control approaches using imitation learning, muscle synergy, and model-based reinforcement learning, with reported performance exceeding the provided baseline by a factor of ten. Through MyoSuite's open-source simulation framework, standardized tasks, and physiologically realistic models, the benchmark supplies a reproducible setting for studying machine learning and biomechanics together.
neurips-2025-myochallenge-2024-a-new-ben.tldr: MyoChallenge benchmarks joint biological-prosthetic control through simulated manipulation and locomotion tasks, with competition methods substantially exceeding its baseline.

paragraphs: The paper develops automated bidding algorithms for repeated first-price auctions subject to return-on-investment constraints. Its focus is a difficult setting where the auction mechanism does not make truthful bidding the natural solution. The bidder must learn over time while respecting the financial constraint on the bidding strategy.

The algorithms are compared with the best randomized strategy chosen in hindsight. This is a stronger benchmark than the weaker comparisons used by some earlier work on non-truthful auctions. Regret measures the accumulated performance shortfall against that benchmark, so a sublinear bound means the average shortfall per auction decreases as the number of auctions grows.

When the bidder observes the maximum competing bid, the algorithm achieves a near-optimal regret bound of roughly the square root of T, ignoring logarithmic factors. With only win-or-loss feedback, the bound is roughly T to the three-quarters power. Here T is the number of auctions. These results establish no-regret learning under both feedback settings while showing how the stated guarantees depend on the information available.
neurips-2025-no-regret-online-autobiddin.tldr: The paper gives no-regret bidding algorithms for ROI-constrained first-price auctions against the best randomized strategy in hindsight.

paragraphs: Structural causal bandits use causal graphs to help choose interventions, reducing the need to try actions that cannot be optimal. This paper extends that idea to environments whose causal mechanisms evolve over time. In these settings, judging an intervention only by its immediate reward can miss consequences that affect later decisions.

The proposed framework uses temporal structural causal models to represent how interventions and information propagate across time. The authors develop graphical tools and assumptions for reasoning about those effects. They also introduce POMIS+, extending the idea of possibly optimal minimal intervention sets to capture variables that contribute to maximizing immediate and longer-term rewards.

This changes intervention selection from a static comparison into a temporally aware decision problem. The framework explicitly represents delayed effects so that potentially useful interventions can be considered in light of their broader consequences. Empirical evaluations show improved performance over myopic baselines. Those results support the practical value of the temporal formulation in the studied settings, alongside its theoretical contribution to organizing intervention choices.
neurips-2025-non-stationary-structural-c.tldr: A temporal causal-bandit framework accounts for delayed intervention effects and improves on myopic baselines in empirical evaluations.

paragraphs: Generalist anomaly detection trains a single model that can identify unusual examples in new domains. Earlier approaches mainly guide detection with normal reference samples. This paper studies a setting where anomalous references are also available and uses both kinds of examples to provide a richer basis for deciding what is abnormal.

The proposed NAGL framework has two components. Residual Mining extracts abnormal patterns from differences between normal and anomalous references, building representations intended to transfer across domains. Anomaly Feature Learning then uses residual mapping to adapt anomaly features to the query image. The first component learns useful reference differences; the second connects those differences to the particular image being examined.

Across multiple benchmarks, the method significantly outperforms existing generalist anomaly detection approaches. The authors also describe the approach as more accurate and efficient across domains. Its central contribution is making anomalous reference examples part of generalist detection, with the intended practical setting explicitly including access to both normal and abnormal samples.
neurips-2025-normal-abnormal-guided-gene.tldr: NAGL uses differences between normal and anomalous references to improve anomaly detection across domains.

paragraphs: Position encoding gives attention mechanisms information about sequence structure. In rotary position encoding, or RoPE, the transformation relating two positions depends on their relative distance and is otherwise independent of the input. PaTH changes this by making the positional transformation depend on the data being processed.

The method accumulates products of input-dependent Householder-like transformations. This makes the relationship between sequence elements more expressive than one determined solely by distance. To make the approach practical to train, the authors exploit a compact representation of these matrix products to derive an efficient parallel algorithm. They also implement a blockwise computation in the style of FlashAttention.

PaTH improves on RoPE and other recent baselines in targeted synthetic tests and moderate-scale language modeling experiments. The authors further show that pretrained RoPE transformers can be converted to PaTH through continued pretraining. These findings support input-dependent position encoding as a useful design direction, with evidence covering both newly evaluated models and adaptation of already pretrained transformers.
neurips-2025-path-attention-position-enc.tldr: PaTH makes position encoding input-dependent and improves on RoPE in synthetic and moderate-scale language modeling experiments.

paragraphs: PathVQ addresses the cost of preserving detailed visual information in pathology whole-slide analysis. A common efficient approach represents each image tile using one summary token. The authors find that spatial patch tokens contain useful additional information, but retaining all of them can increase computation and storage by up to roughly 200 times.

The proposed framework compresses patch features through vector quantization, storing discrete indices and reconstructing features with a decoder. It reports 64-fold compression, from 1,024 to 16 dimensions, while preserving fidelity. A multi-scale quantization strategy further improves reconstruction and supplies self-supervised training signals for learning representations of entire slides.

Using those compressed features and supervision signals, the authors build a progressive convolutional module and a slide-level self-supervised objective. The goal is to retain rich spatial information without the full cost of using every original patch feature. Experiments across multiple datasets achieve reported state-of-the-art performance, supporting compression as a way to make detailed slide representations more scalable and effective for downstream pathology tasks.
neurips-2025-pathvq-reforming-computatio.tldr: PathVQ compresses spatial patch features to make rich whole-slide pathology representations more efficient while achieving strong downstream performance.

paragraphs: R²ec investigates how a large recommendation model can combine explicit reasoning with efficient item prediction. Language models already support recommendation through representations or generated items, but adding reasoning creates a need to train and execute both capabilities together. The paper proposes a unified model designed around that combination.

Its dual-head architecture supports reasoning-chain generation and item prediction within one model, substantially reducing inference latency according to the authors. To address the shortage of annotated reasoning examples, the paper introduces RecPO, a reinforcement learning framework. A fused reward mechanism jointly optimizes reasoning and recommendation, tying training to both parts of the model's intended behavior.

Across three datasets, R²ec outperforms traditional recommenders, language-model-based recommenders, and reasoning-augmented baselines. Further analysis finds competitive efficiency relative to conventional language-model recommenders and strong adaptability across recommendation scenarios. The contribution therefore combines architecture and training: a shared model supports both outputs, while joint reward optimization develops the reasoning and recommendation capabilities without relying on annotated reasoning data.
neurips-2025-r-2-ec-towards-large-recomm.tldr: R²ec jointly trains reasoning and recommendation in a dual-head model, improving tested recommendation performance with competitive inference efficiency.

paragraphs: REP targets the resource cost of prompt-based continual learning for vision. These methods learn from changing data without rehearsing earlier examples, but strong predictive performance can still come with substantial computation and memory requirements. The paper aims to reduce those requirements while keeping accuracy trade-offs small.

The framework combines swift prompt selection with adaptive token merging and adaptive layer dropping. Prompt selection refines input data using a carefully provisioned model. During prompt updates, token merging reduces the data processed, while layer dropping selectively skips model layers. These adaptive mechanisms seek to retain features relevant to the current task as new tasks are learned.

Experiments across multiple image classification datasets show better resource efficiency than state-of-the-art rehearsal-free continual learning methods. The contribution addresses more than the size of the learned prompts: it also changes how much data and model computation each update uses. The reported findings support selective processing as a practical way to reduce the cost of adapting vision models to changing tasks.
neurips-2025-rep-resource-efficient-prom.tldr: REP reduces the resource demands of rehearsal-free continual learning through efficient prompt selection, adaptive token merging, and layer dropping.

paragraphs: The paper studies quantile estimation using repeated resamples much smaller than the original dataset, drawn without replacement. Such resampling is useful in large-sample inference, but the authors identify a gap in rigorous guarantees that avoid unknown nuisance parameters. Their analysis supplies those guarantees for a fully data-driven estimator.

First, they prove a central limit theorem under a mild moment condition, giving an asymptotic distribution without unknown nuisance parameters. They then construct a counterexample where the theorem fails, showing that the moment requirement is essentially tight. This is a substantive boundary on the result: the guarantee depends on a condition that cannot simply be removed in general.

Under slightly stronger assumptions, an Edgeworth expansion yields exact convergence rates, and a Berry–Esséen bound quantifies bootstrap approximation error. The authors also derive parameter-free asymptotic distributions for practical statistics, including quantiles associated with random-walk Metropolis–Hastings and rewards in ergodic Markov decision processes. These applications connect the theoretical error guarantees to estimation problems involving stochastic computation and learning.
neurips-2025-small-resamples-sharp-guara.tldr: The paper proves parameter-free asymptotic guarantees and convergence rates for resampled quantile estimators under explicit moment assumptions.

paragraphs: Thousand Voices of Trauma addresses the limited availability of therapy conversation data for trauma-focused research. It provides 3,000 synthetic conversations based on Prolonged Exposure therapy protocols for post-traumatic stress disorder. The dataset covers 500 distinct cases, each represented through six conversational perspectives.

Those perspectives reflect a progression from initial anxiety through peak distress to emotional processing. The generation process combines deterministic and probabilistic methods and includes varied demographic profiles, 20 trauma types, and 10 trauma-related behaviors. This design gives researchers multiple views of each case while building variation into both the represented experiences and their conversational expression.

Clinical experts assessed the dataset's therapeutic fidelity, recognizing emotional depth while recommending refinements for greater authenticity. The authors also introduce an emotional trajectory benchmark with standardized measures for evaluating model responses. Together, the synthetic conversations and evaluation framework provide a privacy-preserving research resource for modeling trauma-focused dialogue, with intended uses in patient-facing applications and clinician training tools. The expert feedback also identifies authenticity as an area for further refinement.
neurips-2025-thousand-voices-of-trauma-a.tldr: The paper introduces 3,000 synthetic trauma-therapy conversations and an emotional trajectory benchmark, with expert validation and suggested authenticity refinements.

paragraphs: This paper builds an image tokenizer around a frozen vision foundation model. The tokenizer converts visual information into tokens for autoregressive image generation, while keeping its pretrained encoder unchanged. The approach explores how existing visual representations can support both efficient tokenization and high-quality image synthesis.

Two components adapt those representations to the task. Region-adaptive quantization reduces redundancy in features arranged on a regular two-dimensional grid. A semantic reconstruction objective aligns tokenizer outputs with the foundation model's representations, helping preserve meaningful visual content. Together, these designs address both how compactly an image is represented and how faithfully its semantics survive the conversion.

The authors report improvements in reconstruction, generation quality, and token efficiency. On ImageNet benchmarks, the resulting autoregressive generation system achieves a gFID of 1.36 and threefold faster convergence. It also supports high-fidelity class-conditional generation without classifier-free guidance. These results show that a frozen visual encoder, paired with suitable quantization and reconstruction objectives, can provide an effective foundation for image tokenization.
neurips-2025-vision-foundation-models-as.tldr: A tokenizer built on a frozen vision foundation model improves image generation and token efficiency through adaptive quantization and semantic reconstruction.
